source.title: Linear RNNs Provably Learn Linear Dynamical Systems
source.authors: Li-Fu Wang; Tianyu Wang; Shengwei Yi; Bo Shen; Bo Hu; Xing Cao

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no obvious cutoff or garbling that prevents extracting the main results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical gradient-descent training guarantees for linear RNNs on stable linear dynamical systems, a new setting relative to the claim’s benchmark and architecture-specific versions.
record.gate_note: The results are theoretical guarantees for excess loss on stable linear systems, not measured CIFAR classification errors. The paper also cites findings from prior work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional optimization and generalization guarantees for linear RNNs learning stable linear systems. These results measure none of V1–V6: they do not establish benchmark classification error, ReLU spurious-minimum frequencies, depth degradation, comparative initialization benefits, stability-threshold dynamics, or normalization benefits. Its discussion of V2's original source supplies no new test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the stated stability, width, loss, data, and prescribed random-initialization conditions, SGD learns stable linear systems with polynomial iteration and sample bounds, and required hidden width independent of sequence length. This is a theoretical guarantee, not empirical evidence about practical RNN training generally.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes linear RNNs learning stable linear dynamical systems with convex loss, rather than large non-convex networks’ benchmark classification error. It gives theoretical guarantees rather than measured CIFAR results.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee depends on the stated stable-system conditions, width threshold, initialization, and loss assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 4 bounds average sampled excess loss by O(ϵ) for sufficiently wide linear RNNs trained with SGD under prescribed initialization, stability, bounded-data, and loss assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, SGD on sufficiently wide linear RNNs achieves O(ϵ) average excess loss relative to a stable linear target, with required width independent of sequence length.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 6 provides an O(ϵ) population-versus-sampled excess-loss bound under the theorem's conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The specified linear-RNN learning procedure admits a conditional generalization guarantee, yielding a population-loss learning guarantee when combined with its optimization bound.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications
record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and conditional on the paper’s stability, loss, width, and initialization assumptions; it does not empirically measure training classification error on benchmarks.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying study results were identified. Results cited from prior studies were excluded.

untested.parts: All: convolutional networks, CIFAR classification training error, random labels, and model-size or training-recipe effects.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
All: depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization and normalization exceptions.

All: comparative effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons. Proving convergence for one prescribed initialization does not test these effects.
All: learning rates relative to initial or evolving stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes, and divergence.
All: normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Neither row's original observed state should be interpreted as observing an effect in V1–V6. No verdict labels apply, and no additional results bearing on these versions were identified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional networks, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional network depth, shortcuts, and the stated initialization or normalization comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization, signal or gradient propagation in plain networks, and the stated tanh and convolutional depth comparisons.
Learning rates above or below stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
Batch normalization’s effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

rows.measure: Average empirical excess loss over the target system’s loss
rows.note: A theoretical guarantee, not a measured benchmark result. The bound is on average loss relative to the target system, not classification error.
rows.check: The guarantee cannot determine any listed version. Equation (12) bounds excess loss averaged over successive SGD iterates and their sampled sequences, rather than training loss of a final model on a fixed dataset. Its comparator is an admissible stable target system; OPTρC is the population comparator used elsewhere.

source_check.correct: Equation (12) subtracts the target system's loss on each sampled sequence, averaged over time and SGD iterates. OPTρC, defined in Eq. (6), is instead the infimum population loss over admissible target systems.
source_check.locator_found: Section II, Eq. (6); Section V, Theorem 4, Eq. (12); Section VII, Theorem 15, Eq. (28).
source_check.problem: The baseline parenthetical conflates sampled target-system loss with the optimal population loss OPTρC.
